newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: F&P sees flat outlook amid weak NZ market.
newsitem.headline: F&P sees flat outlook amid weak NZ market.

text.p: New Zealand-based appliance manufacturer Fisher & Paykel said on Friday it expected to report a profit for the current year at a similar level to the NZ$37.2 million net profit it made in the year to end March.

In a statement alongside its 1996/97 results the company said that "given the difficult economic outlook in the company's main markets and a continuation of the trends experienced in the second half of the financial year, the directors at this time anticipate a similar result to last year."

It expected continued growth in Australian whiteware and in heathcare sales overseas, but noted consumer demand for durable products in New Zealand was expected to remain "at the weaker levels experienced since October 1996 due to lack of consumer confidence and generally low levels of economic activity".

Looking at last year's markets generally, F&P said "whiteware competition in Australia, New Zealand and other export markets was intense with trading conditions deteriorating during the year and market sizes for most products reducing.
"Notwithstanding this, market shares progressively increased in Australia and New Zealand," it added.
F&P said it would continue to emphasise its "cost innovation" programme intended to minimise the adverse impact of intensified trading conditions and improve its cost competivity.

It felt that even though its profits fell by 5.3 percent in the year to this March its "relatively sound performance demonstrates the underlying strength of the company, its ability to react quickly to changes in business and market conditions ...and strong retailer support".
The company's shares were indicated lower than Thursday's close of NZ$5.11 after the results, but by 2300 GMT no shares had been traded. --Wellington newsroom +64 4 471 4273
